text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Armed gangsters raid Kenol trading Centre in Maragua District (Central Province), killing two people and injuring at least 10.

- The National Opposition Alliance vows not to participate in next year's General Elections if there is no independent electoral commission and a review of parliamentary and civic electoral boundaries based on population.
- Kenya Airways announces it will not pay a dividend this year although it has made a record operating profit of two billion shillings from a turnover of 10 billion shillings.
- The Secretary-General of the FORD-Asili faction Martin Shikuku rules out returning to the historic Kamukunji grounds in Nairobi, on November 16 to agitate for constitutional reforms.

- A special report compiled by the management of the giant dairy cooperative, Kenya Cooperative Creameries (KCC) says the company faces a financial crisis owing to escalating processing and packaging costs and its inability to market its products.

- Education Minister Joseph Kamotho accuses the Catholic Church of dishonesty saying his ministry had discovered that Catholic authors had published books on sex education for the youth and yet the church had criticised his ministry for introducing the teaching of family life education in schools.
